reason: No heating in cold weather. The living room was 10°C at 16:25 (event-18). The tenant has a mobility impairment (event-3), her only heater is unsafe (event-8, event-12, event-13), and she has no workable interim warmth. Policy treats no heating in cold weather with a vulnerable occupant as P1 and escalates it. Nobody has authority over temporary heating, transport or accommodation: the £250 authority excludes them (event-7) and the duty file records no separate limit (event-17). The landlord is travelling and has not addressed interim measures (event-10, event-14), so a person must decide. The diagnostic itself is covered. The landlord confirmed in event-14 that the £250 urgent-repair authority covers the £168 call-out, and event-19 shows the same £168 fixed fee, diagnostic only, for the 15 Jan 09:00-11:00 slot. I checked property, provider, amount and agency against the job and found no mismatch. I staged an instruction to Brackenridge to book that slot, and it must be confirmed by 17:30. I made no promise on repair costs and said any work needs written confirmation. The tenant already said she can give access on 15 Jan with 30 minutes' notice and a direct call (event-13), but she has not confirmed this specific slot, so I asked her to. I staged an update to her with no promise on interim help. I did not choose a routine step alone, because the interim-care gap and the vulnerable occupant need human judgement. Event-19 is not a risk to the instruction: the slot has not been booked yet. A routine WAIT would be wrong given the 17:30 deadline. The decision would change if the landlord approves interim spend, or if the provider cannot hold the slot.
